author: Robert Carr
description: A substantial beef and barley soup with deeply browned mushrooms, porcini, thyme and a small miso-balsamic finish. Lean ground beef gives reliable tenderness without a long stew-meat braise.
equipment: 8-quart Dutch oven or heavy soup pot with lid
Fine-mesh strainer lined with a coffee filter

18 g; choose 650 mg sodium or less per tbsp

ingredients: 1 1/2 lb (680 g) 95% lean ground beef
2 tbsp (27 g) extra-virgin olive oil, divided into three 2-tsp portions
1 lb (454 g) cremini mushrooms, cleaned, dried and thickly sliced
1/2 oz (14 g) dried porcini mushrooms
2 cups (480 mL) boiling water for the porcini; after filtering, add water only to restore the soaking liquid to 2 cups (480 mL)
1 large yellow onion (250 g peeled), diced
2 medium carrots (200 g trimmed), cut into 1/4-inch dice
3 celery stalks (150 g trimmed), cut into 1/4-inch dice
5 garlic cloves (16 g peeled), minced
2 tbsp (32 g) no-salt-added tomato paste
1 tsp dried thyme
2 bay leaves
1 cup (200 g) dry pearl barley, rinsed; not hulled or quick-cooking barley
6 cups (1.44 L) low-sodium beef broth, with 140 mg sodium or less per cup
1 tbsp (15 mL) Worcestershire sauce
1 tbsp (18 g) white miso, with 650 mg sodium or less per tbsp
1 tbsp (15 mL) balsamic vinegar
1/2 cup (20 g) chopped flat-leaf parsley
1/2 tsp (3 g) fine sea salt, divided into two 1/4-tsp portions
1/2 tsp black pepper, divided into two 1/4-tsp portions
instructions: Cover 1/2 oz (14 g) dried porcini with 2 cups (480 mL) boiling water in a heatproof bowl. Soak for 15 minutes while you begin browning the beef. Lift out the porcini, rinse off any grit, and chop finely. Filter the soaking liquid through a coffee-filter-lined strainer into a measuring jug, leaving grit behind. Add water only until the filtered liquid measures 2 cups (480 mL).

Heat 2 tsp (9 g) olive oil in an 8-quart pot over medium-high heat. Add 1 1/2 lb (680 g) lean ground beef, 1/4 tsp (1.5 g) fine sea salt, and 1/4 tsp black pepper. Press the beef into a broad layer and leave it for 3-4 minutes to brown. Turn in sections, break into bite-size crumbles, and cook for 4-5 minutes, until browned and the largest clumps reach 160 F (71 C). Transfer the beef and its juices to a bowl. Do not discard the brown coating on the pot.

Add 2 tsp (9 g) olive oil and 1 lb (454 g) sliced cremini mushrooms to the pot. Cook over medium-high heat for 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until released liquid has evaporated and the mushrooms have deeply browned edges. Reduce the heat if the coating on the pot threatens to burn; pale, watery mushrooms are not finished.

Reduce the heat to medium. Add 2 tsp (9 g) olive oil, 1 diced onion (250 g), 2 diced carrots (200 g), 3 diced celery stalks (150 g), and 1/4 tsp (1.5 g) fine sea salt. Cook for 6-8 minutes, stirring, until softened. Stir in 2 tbsp (32 g) tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes. Add 5 minced garlic cloves (16 g) and 1 tsp dried thyme; stir for 30 seconds.

Add 6 cups (1.44 L) low-sodium beef broth and the measured 2 cups (480 mL) filtered porcini liquid. Scrape up the brown coating. Stir in the chopped porcini from the 14 g dry batch, 1 cup (200 g) rinsed pearl barley, 2 bay leaves, 1 tbsp (15 mL) Worcestershire sauce, and all browned beef from the 680 g raw batch with its juices. Bring to a boil, then simmer gently with the lid slightly ajar for 35-45 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes, until the barley is pleasantly chewy with no hard center. Start checking at 30 minutes; barley brands and simmer intensity vary.

Remove the 2 bay leaves. Take 1/2 cup (120 mL) hot broth out of the soup and whisk it with 1 tbsp (18 g) white miso in a bowl until smooth. Turn off the heat and return that mixture to the pot; this is broth taken from the batch, not extra broth. Stir in 1 tbsp (15 mL) balsamic vinegar, 1/2 cup (20 g) chopped parsley, and 1/4 tsp black pepper. Rest for 5 minutes, then divide the complete batch evenly among 6 servings, distributing beef, mushrooms and barley evenly.
notes: Flavor: properly browned beef and mushrooms, filtered porcini broth, brick-red tomato paste and thyme supply the savory base. The small miso dose rounds it out, while balsamic brightens the finish without turning the soup into a sweet glaze. Do not add bouillon cubes or extra salt automatically.

Health-conscious design: use 95% lean beef rather than fatty mince or sausage. Mushrooms and barley add substantial volume and fiber; oil, miso, Worcestershire and salt are measured. Pearl barley is not a whole grain, although it supplies fiber. Hulled barley is a different product with a longer cooking time and is not a direct timed substitution here.

The timing intentionally allows a proper barley simmer and mushroom browning. This is not a 30-minute soup. White miso, Worcestershire and broth all contribute sodium; choose the specified labels and do not assume an unsalted stock is sodium-free. This recipe is not certified low sodium.

Meal prep: divide into 6 shallow containers and refrigerate at 40 F (4 C) or below within 2 hours, or within 1 hour above 90 F (32 C). Do not wait for the entire pot to cool on the counter. Use refrigerated portions within 3-4 days; freeze portions intended for later days on prep day, leaving expansion room. Plan to use frozen portions within 3 months for quality. Thaw overnight in the refrigerator.

Barley continues absorbing liquid. Reheat one portion with 1/4 cup (60 mL) water, stirring often, until the soup briefly reaches a rolling boil and the center reaches 165 F (74 C). For a still-thick portion, add a second 2 tbsp (30 mL) water and heat through again. For microwave reheating, cover loosely, stir halfway and check several spots reach 165 F (74 C).

Allergens: barley contains gluten; miso contains soy and may also contain barley; Worcestershire commonly contains fish and may contain wheat. Check all packaged labels. Tap water used for soaking and reheating is intentionally not a grocery purchase.
Developed and reviewed in writing; not yet kitchen-tested. Numerical nutrition estimates are not published because final product labels and a complete calculation have not been verified.
